headline: With 0 runs in the last 28 days and 15 weeks until the 10 km goal, the priority is to restart consistently and build cautiously rather than judge fitness.

to_improve.meaning: There is time to make progress, but the outcome will depend more on accumulating regular run/walk sessions than on trying to make up for the recent gap with hard or long runs.

stamina: Build stamina by first establishing repeatable run/walk sessions, not by testing how far you can run continuously. Since the data shows 0 runs in the last 28 days, treat each planned session as practice for returning to regular running. Keep the run portions controlled, take the planned walk breaks, and allow recovery between sessions. When the current plan is consistently manageable, progress only as the plan prescribes. There is no recent longest run, pace, heart-rate, terrain, sleep, fatigue, or pain data, so it is not possible to set a safe starting interval or distance from this information alone.
cautions: A rapid jump from 0 recent runs to frequent, long, or hard running could raise injury risk.
Persistent pain is a reason to see a qualified professional rather than train through it.
